== New Individual Sessions report

The Individual Sessions report lists every session started within a selected date range, one row per session, with session timing, user, team, device details, session minutes, type, and state.

- Available under *Analytics Reports* in the Portal to organization ADMINs only, in the *Usage* group.
- The date range defaults to the last 7 days.
- Filter by *Date Range*, *Team*, or *User Email*. *User Email* accepts multiple addresses and searches the full user list as you type.
- The table displays up to 100,000 rows. For larger result sets, narrow the filters or export the report to CSV.

See xref:reporting:individual-sessions-report.adoc[].

// Source: KOB-55750 from PR #917
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/917

== Private mode pauses recording in automation sessions

Turn on private mode in a Xium or basic Appium 2 automation session to pause recording while your script handles private data.

- Turn on private mode with the `kobiton:privateMode` capability at session start, or turn it on and off during the session with the `Update Settings` Appium command.
- While private mode is on, screenshots, Appium and Xium logs, device logs, WebDriver traffic, view trees, system metrics, and network capture are not recorded. Commands run during this time are hidden in Session Explorer, and the session video skips the private part.
- Errors are still returned to the script, and crash logs are still collected.
- Recording resumes when private mode is turned off. Sessions that never turn on private mode are recorded as before.

For details and limitations, see xref:automation-testing:scripting/obfuscate-private-data-in-appium-script.adoc[].

// Source: KOB-53795 from PR #905

== App uploads no longer stay in Parsing

Each app upload now finishes parsing or ends in a parsing failure. In the Kobiton API, the app version `state` moves from `PARSING` to `OK` or `FAILURE_PARSING`.

* If the uploaded file can't be read, the app version shows a parsing failure.
* If parsing can't start after the upload, the app version is marked as a parsing failure.
* An app or app version that is waiting to be parsed can be deleted from the Portal.
* The *Delete* button for an app in *Parsing* now appears after 1 hour instead of 15 minutes.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-53795): Confirm the Portal label of the button that appears for an app stuck in Parsing. The source calls it *Delete*; the Manage apps page documents *Remove App*.

// Source: KOB-55365 from PR #932
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/932

== Accurate install errors for iOS apps built with an App Store distribution profile

Installing an iOS app built with an App Store distribution profile no longer returns an incorrect AD-403 error asking you to re-upload a development build.

* When the install fails, the error reported by the device is shown instead, such as a code signature verification failure.
* When *App signing using Kobiton Certificate (iOS)* is turned off, these apps are no longer rejected before installation.

// Source: KOB-56015 from PR #914
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/914

== Live view stays current on Android devices with Lightning Mode off

In manual sessions on Android devices with *Lightning Mode* off, the live view now updates as the device screen changes. Previously, the live view could keep showing an earlier screen until you tapped it.

* Screen changes that happen on their own, such as a running stopwatch, appear in the live view without a tap.
* *Home*, *Back*, *Power*, and *Recent apps* on the session toolbar show their result in the live view right away.
* After you tap the live view, it shows the screen the tap led to, not the screen from before the tap.

// Source: KOB-55512 from PR #912
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/912

== Standard W3C errors for Selenium Java clients in Xium sessions

Xium automation sessions started with Selenium 3 or Selenium 4 Java clients, including Appium Java client 10, now return standard W3C WebDriver errors. For example, a missing element raises `NoSuchElementException` instead of a general `WebDriverException`, and client logs no longer show `incorrect JSON status mapping`. Sessions that use only `desiredCapabilities` and basic Appium 2 sessions are unchanged.

// Source: KOB-55810 from PR #926
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/926

== Text entry into covered fields in iOS Xium sessions

In iOS Xium sessions, tapping, clearing, or typing into an element now succeeds when iOS can't scroll the element into view. For example, the on-screen keyboard can cover a password or PIN field on an iPad in landscape orientation, in an app whose form uses its own scrolling instead of the standard iOS scrolling.

* The session scrolls the element's nearest scrollable container until the element can be reached, then completes the action.
* If the element still can't be reached after three scroll attempts, the session returns the `kAXErrorCannotComplete` error.
* Elements that are already visible, or that iOS can scroll into view, are not affected.

// Source: KOB-55783 from PR #908
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/908

== Accurate no-device messages for sessions started by device tags

When a session request selects devices by tag and no device is available, the reason in the error message is now based only on devices that have the requested tags. Previously, the reason could come from any device that matched the other capabilities, including devices without the requested tags.

* If a device with the requested tags matches the request but is in use, the message states that the matching devices are currently in use.
* If no device matches the requested tags, the message states `There are no devices that satisfy your filter criteria`. Requests that previously returned a "currently in use" message because of a device without the requested tags now return this message instead.

This applies to Appium sessions that use `kobiton:deviceTags` and to Turbo Test sessions started by device tags. Device selection is unchanged. A session started by device tags runs on the same device as before.

// Source: KOB-55511 from PR #918
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/918

== More reliable WEBVIEW discovery in Android mixed sessions

On Android devices, each Appium session that runs during the same mixed session now lists the `WEBVIEW` context for a web page open in Chrome, including pages in a Chrome Custom Tab such as Auth0 sign-in pages. Previously, only the first Appium session listed the `WEBVIEW` context. Later Appium sessions in the same mixed session returned only `NATIVE_APP`, without an error.

Mixed sessions that include only one Appium session behave as before. iOS sessions are unaffected.

// Source: KOB-56321 from PR #928
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/928

== Reliable screen reads on iOS 15 devices

Screen reads now complete reliably on iOS 15 devices, including the XML hierarchy captured around each action in a manual session, Appium element searches and page source requests, and Network Payload Capture setup.

// Source: KOB-55761 from PR #907
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/907

== Kobiton CLI prevents commands from acting on the wrong session

Kobiton CLI commands that pass `-s <SESSION_ID>` with a session token for a different session now fail with an error that identifies the token to pass, instead of acting on the wrong session.

Previously, with more than one CLI session open, parts of a command that passed `-s` without a matching token could apply to the most recently created session instead of the one named.

- Each open session needs its own session token, passed with `-a <SESSION_TOKEN>` or the `KOBITON_SESSION_TOKEN` environment variable.
- Help for `-a`, `-s`, `kobiton session create`, and `--hide` now describes this requirement.
- With a single session open, commands run without `-a` or `-s` work as before.

For details, see xref:kobiton-cli:use-the-cli.adoc#session-context[Use session context consistently].

// Source: KOB-56011 from PR #901
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/901

== deviceConnect hosts reconnect after restart

Restarted and newly started deviceConnect hosts now connect normally. Previously, hosts that restarted after the November 6, 2026 release could not reconnect, which left their devices offline.

// Source: KOB-56018 from PR #922
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/922

== deviceConnect Console device list loads with provisioning profiles from more than one team

The device list in deviceConnect Console now loads, and other Console pages and API requests respond, when an iOS device is covered by provisioning profiles from more than one Apple Developer team.

* When a newer provisioning profile from a different team covers the device, the agent apps are re-signed with that profile once, and the signed copy is reused after that.
* Re-signing of your iOS apps can also use a newer provisioning profile from a different team than the one the app was last signed with. Profiles that lack a capability your app requires are still not used.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-56018): The ticket's impact analysis states that re-signing customer apps can use a profile from a different team. The recorded test results cover the deviceConnect agent apps only. Confirm the second bullet before publication.

// Source: KOB-55655 from PR #924

== New Android devices appear right away while USB debugging is unauthorized

A new Android device connected to a deviceConnect host now appears in the device list right away, even before USB debugging is allowed on the device. Until you allow USB debugging, the device shows an error status, such as `Device inaccessible: Unauthorized` or `Device inaccessible: Authorizing`. Previously, the device could take up to 10 minutes to appear.

== deviceConnect Console connection status

deviceConnect Console now shows in its header whether deviceConnect is connected to Kobiton and to gigacap. Connection problems can be identified at a glance without reading deviceConnect logs.

- A status dot and label for *Kobiton* and *gigacap* appear next to the user menu for users with System Configuration access. Hover over a status to see its state and the reason for it.
- Each service shows one of these states: *Online*, *Offline*, *Error*, or *Not Configured*.
- *Kobiton* shows *Error* when the tenant API key in `dc.ini` is rejected, for example a wrong key or a key that belongs to another account. The hover text shows the reason, such as `Invalid username or apikey/password`.
- *Kobiton* shows *Not Configured* when `ApiBaseUrl` or a linked tenant is not set. *gigacap* shows *Not Configured* when no GEM redirect is configured.
- Status changes appear automatically, without reloading the page.
- The status dots turn gray while the console is disconnected from deviceConnect, such as during a service restart, and show the current state again when the connection returns.
- In windows narrower than 1200 pixels, only the status dots appear.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55656): The deviceConnect release version that includes this change is not stated in the ticket. Confirm the version and whether this entry belongs on the Standalone, Cloud, or both release pages before publishing.
